items.h: Kenneth Walker III (groin) misses walkthrough Monday
items.s: Kenneth Walker III did not participate in Monday's walkthrough practice. It is a short week for the Chiefs on Thursday against the Bills. Walker will need to continue to be monitored in practice on Tuesday after missing the past two weeks.

items.h: Deemed 'DNP' on practice estimate
items.s: Walker (groin) was listed as a non-participant on Monday's practice estimate. Since the Chiefs are coming off a 34-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday, the team held a walk-through Monday in preparation for Thursday's game against the Bills. Nate Taylor of ESPN.com previously reported that the Chiefs were "optimistic" that Walker could be available for the team's Thanksgiving night contest, but with one 'DNP' now on the books, the running back has two more opportunities to log any listed level of practice participation before the team posts its Week 12 game statuses.

items.h: Kenneth Walker Misses Practice on Monday
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker (groin) was estimated as a non-participant in practice on Monday, according to the team. A groin injury kept Walker sidelined for a second straight game in Sunday's Week 11 blowout win over the visiting Arizona Cardinals, and he is on the wrong track to return for a Thanksgiving Day showdown against the Buffalo Bills this Thursday after missing the first practice of the week. The Chiefs are definitely not in a rush to bring the 26-year-old back too soon after rookie Emmett Johnson has produced 206 rushing yards and a touchdown on 45 carries while catching 10 of 11 targets for 108 yards and two receiving touchdowns in the last two games with…

items.h: Kenneth Walker Will Remain Chiefs Starter When Healthy
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker (groin) has missed the past two games with a groin injury, and in his absence, rookie Emmett Johnson has racked up 314 total yards and three touchdowns, twice turning in a top-six fantasy finish. While fantasy managers have speculated what a workload split might look like upon Walker's return, offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy left little doubt about the hierarchy of the room when speaking with the media on Monday. "Kenneth is the starter. If Kenneth is to play, he'll remain the starter," he told reporters. "We're coaching that next man to be prepared to be the man. Emmett has done a great job, but we also understand the value that Kenneth…

items.h: Kenneth Walker III (groin) ruled out for Sunday
items.s: Kenneth Walker III (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals. The Chiefs are letting Walker sit out for a second-straight game as he continues to nurse a groin injury that he recently suffered. It's not considered a serious issue at this point, however, so he seems to have a chance to play in Week 12's matchup against the Bills next Thursday night. Emmett Johnson was dominant as the Chiefs' RB1 last week and will be a must-start fantasy option in a favorable matchup against the Cardinals this week.

items.h: Ruled out for Sunday's game
items.s: Walker (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals. Walker, who wasn't able to practice this week, will thus target a potential return Thursday against the Bills. With the Chiefs erring on the side of caution with Walker with a short week ahead, Emmett Johnson -- who rushed 22 times for 101 yards and brought in six of seven targets for 70 yards and TDs in the team's Week 10 win over the Falcons -- is headed toward a second consecutive start this weekend.

items.h: Likely out in Week 11
items.s: Head coach Andy Reid said Friday that Walker (groin) "most likely" won't be available Sunday against the Cardinals, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports. Walker showed up at the Chiefs' facilities last Friday with a tight groin and eventually was ruled out for this past Sunday's game in Atlanta. With no practice reps to speak of yet during Week 11 prep, he appears to be trending toward another absence this Sunday, which again will thrust rookie Emmett Johnson into a workhorse role out of Kansas City's backfield.

items.h: Not spotted Friday
items.s: Walker (groin) wasn't spotted during the portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star reports. Walker hasn't practiced at all this week and should be expected to be ruled out for Sunday's game against Arizona later Friday. With the Cardinals bringing their minor-league team to Kansas City this weekend, there's no reason to push Walker when the Chiefs have a quick Week 12 turnaround with a game against the Bills on Thanksgiving. Emmett Johnson will be a top fantasy RB for Week 11 once Walker is officially ruled out.

items.h: Kenneth Walker Ruled Out But is "Improving"
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said that running back Kenneth Walker (groin) will be listed as out for Sunday's Week 11 game against the visiting Arizona Cardinals, according to Nate Taylor of ESPN. However, Reid said that Walker is "improving," which means he could be ready to return for a Thanksgiving Day showdown against the Buffalo Bills next Thursday after a two-game absence. The 26-year-old Walker has not practiced at all this week and will miss a second straight game this weekend. It sets rookie Emmett Johnson up to potentially be an RB1 for a second straight week for fantasy managers after the 23-year-old fifth-rounder from Nebraska had 22 carries for 101 yards and caught…

items.h: Kenneth Walker Absent From Friday's Practice
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker (groin) was not seen at the portion of practice open to the media on Friday, according to Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star. Walker missed last week's blowout win over the Atlanta Falcons and is on his way to being ruled out for a second straight game in Week 11 at home against the Arizona Cardinals. Fantasy managers should be keeping Walker planted on their bench this weekend, with impressive rookie Emmett Johnson having another shot to be an RB1 for fantasy managers. In his first NFL start in place of Walker in Week 10, Johnson went off for 22 carries for 101 yards while adding six receptions on seven targets for 70 yards and two…

items.h: Kenneth Walker III (groin) not practicing Thursday
items.s: Kenneth Walker III remained absent from practice on Thursday. Walker is continuing to trend towards missing a second straight game. He will need to be monitored in practice on Friday.

items.h: Misses Thursday's practice
items.s: Walker (groin) did not practice Thursday. Walker is looking extremely unlikely to play Sunday against a Cardinals team that Kansas City should handle with ease at home. The Chiefs have a quick Week 12 turnaround against the Bills on Thanksgiving, and it may make sense to let Walker rest for another week in preparation for that contest, especially after rookie Emmett Johnson showed in Week 10 against Atlanta that he's more than capable of carrying the torch in the backfield. Fantasy players need to be prepared to be without Walker for at least one more week.

items.h: Kenneth Walker Misses Practice for Second Straight Day Thursday
items.s: For the second straight day, Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker (groin) did not practice on Thursday, according to Adam Schefter of ESPN. Walker came down with a sore groin late last week and did not play in the blowout win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10, and now he is trending toward being held out for a second straight week when the Chiefs host the Arizona Cardinals this Sunday. Walker's injury is not considered long-term, but KC is in no rush to bring him back after rookie Emmett Johnson had 22 carries for 101 yards and six catches for 70 yards and two touchdowns in the 35-13 win over the Falcons in Walker's absence. Walker still has another day to get back on the…

items.h: Kenneth Walker III (groin) not practicing Wednesday
items.s: Kenneth Walker III did not practice on Wednesday. It was reported to begin the week that Walker could sit another game on Sunday. It continues to trend in that direction with Walker missing practice to begin the week.

Walker was sidelined for this past weekend's game against the Falcons, and in his absence rookie Emmett Johnson turned in an impressive performance. Meanwhile, Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site relays that coach Andy Reid said Wednesday that Walker is "feeling a lot better" and that the team…

items.h: Not in line to practice Wednesday
items.s: Walker (groin) won't practice Wednesday, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports. Walker was sidelined for the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons, and in his absence, rookie Emmett Johnson erupted for 171 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns on 28 touches. Now sidelined to begin Week 11 prep, Walker will have two more chances to practice before the Chiefs make a call on his status for Sunday's game against the Cardinals. Walker's sore groin isn't believed to a major concern, and head coach Andy Reid told Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site on Wednesday that the tailback is "feeling a lot better." The Chiefs will see how Walker progresses as the week rolls along, but it…

items.h: Kenneth Walker Will Not Practice Wednesday
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker (groin) will not practice Wednesday, according to head coach Andy Reid and beat writer Pete Sweeney. Walker missed the team's Week 10 win over the Falcons after picking up a mid-week groin injury, and in his absence, rookie Emmett Johnson racked up 171 yards from scrimmage with two touchdowns. Reid noted that his star running back is "feeling a lot better," and the team will see how he progresses over the course of the week. Prior to the injury, Walker was the fantasy RB2, and he belongs in all lineups as soon as he's made available, but should he miss additional games, Johnson can be trusted as a high-end RB2, fully capable of emulating much…

items.h: Kenneth Walker III (groin) could sit Week 11
items.s: Ian Rapoport said he "wouldn't be surprised" if Kenneth Walker sat in Week 11 to make sure that his groin is fully healed. The Chiefs enter this week as huge favorites against the Cardinals. Emmett Johnson could get another week to be in the workhorse role in the Chiefs backfield.

items.h: Kenneth Walker May Sit Another Week
items.s: The Kansas City Chiefs were confident last Saturday that running back Kenneth Walker (groin) would only miss the Week 10 game against the Atlanta Falcons due to a groin injury, but the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport says on Tuesday that he could miss another game because the Chiefs really do not have any reason to rush him back after the way that rookie Emmett Johnson looked in the blowout win over the Falcons. Rapoport said he would not be surprised if the Chiefs keep Walker on the bench for another week for their Week 11 contest against the Arizona Cardinals this Sunday in a game that they can likely win easily without Walker. Fantasy managers who have Johnson rostered would be completely…

items.h: Chiefs Believe Kenneth Walker Has Short-Term Injury
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker (groin) missed the team's Week 10 win over the Falcons with a groin injury, but according to NFL insider Adam Schefter, the team believes it is a short-term ailment. In his absence, rookie Emmett Johnson topped 100 rushing yards for the first time in his career, adding an additional 70 yards and two touchdowns through the air, and it's possible he's earned an expanded role even upon Walker's return. The fantasy RB2 through the first nine weeks of the year, Walker can be plugged back into lineups as soon as he's given the green light, but until that happens, Johnson can be started with confidence and should maintain standalone flex value even…

items.h: Expected back in Week 11
items.s: Walker (groin), who won't play Sunday in Atlanta, is expected to "be able to go" next Sunday against the Cardinals, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Walker showed up at the Chiefs' facilities Friday with a tight groin, didn't take part in the ensuing practice and then was listed as questionable for Week 10 action. The team then ruled him out Saturday, which Rapoport called "more precautionary than anything else." In Walker's absence, rookie fifth-round pick Emmett Johnson is expected to be Kansas City's primary runner.

items.h: Chiefs "Believe" Kenneth Walker Will Return in Week 11
items.s: The Kansas City Chiefs "believe" that running back Kenneth Walker (groin) will return for next Sunday's Week 11 contest against the Arizona Cardinals, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Rapoport reiterated that Walker's groin injury is minor, and although he has already been ruled out for Week 10 against the Atlanta Falcons, he's trending toward missing just the one game. All things considered, that's good news for the Chiefs, who have benefitted from their offseason decision to give Walker a $43.05 million contract last offseason. So far this year, the reigning Super Bowl MVP ranks as the overall RB2 in PPR leagues with 872 rushing yards, 26 catches, 172 receiving yards, and 11…

Walker III will sit out after suffering a groin injury during Thursday's practice session for head coach Andy Reid, with Emmett Johnson in line for a sizeable increase in touches as the No. 1 option out of the Kansas City backfield against the Falcons Sunday.

items.s: Walker (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Jordan Schultz of Fox Sports reports. Walker was a late addition to the Chiefs' practice report Friday as a DNP due to what was described as "groin tightness." Rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson is projected to lead Kansas City's backfield against Atlanta in Walker's absence, and with Jaydn Ott (hamstring) listed as questionable, the Chiefs could elevate Nate Carter from the practice squad to the active roster. Walker's next opportunity to play is…

items.h: Kenneth Walker Ruled Out for Week 10 vs. Falcons
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's Week 10 contest against the Atlanta Falcons, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz. Walker initially injured his groin during practice on Thursday, and while the injury has been described as minor, it was enough to keep him out of practice entirely on Friday. Now, it will also keep him sidelined for Sunday's game, although the good news is that he isn't facing a long-term absence. While the Chiefs don't sound overly concerned about his status going forward, Walker's absence on Sunday could be detrimental for fantasy managers, who were counting on him to continue to contribute as a high-end RB1. Through…

items.h: "Not a Ton of Optimism" for Kenneth Walker's Availability for Sunday
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker's (groin) status is uncertain for a Week 10 game against the Atlanta Falcons due to a groin injury. Walker showed up on Kansas City's injury report on Friday with a sore groin, and he did not participate in practice that day. He is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Falcons. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reported that the Chiefs don't know exactly where Walker stands with the injury, and they will monitor him over the next 24 hours. However, Fowler also reported there is "not a ton of optimism" about Walker's availability, at least as of Friday. Walker currently ranks second in the NFL in rushing yards with 872. If he is…

items.h: Kenneth Walker III (groin) officially questionable for Sunday
items.s: Kenneth Walker III (groin) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons. Walker surprisingly missed Kansas City's practice on Friday due to a groin injury, and that same issue is going to leave him questionable to play heading into the weekend. The team will evaluate his status again closer to game time, and fantasy managers should expect Emmett Johnson to see a large workload and be a good fantasy option if Walker is unable to play against the Falcons this week.

items.h: Deemed questionable for Sunday
items.s: Walker (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Falcons. Walker was added to the Chiefs' Week 10 injury report due to groin tightness that kept him from practicing Friday. Now that he's carrying an official 'questionable' designation heading into the weekend, the running back's status will need to be tracked as Sunday's 1:00 pm ET kickoff approaches. In the event that Walker -- who is averaging a robust 109.0 rushing yards per game and has scored 11 total TDs through eight contests -- is made inactive for the contest, Emmett Johnson would be in line to handle the bulk of the team's carries versus Atlanta.

items.h: Kenneth Walker III (groin) misses practice Friday
items.s: Kenneth Walker III did not practice on Friday. Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Walker came in Friday morning and had "tight groin." "We'll see how he feels through this afternoon, with rehab, and through tomorrow," Reid said. Emmett Johnson should be stashed in all leagues.

items.h: Sits out Friday's practice
items.s: Walker (groin) sat out Friday's practice due to groin tightness, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports. Per McDowell, coach Andy Reid noted of Walker on Friday, "we'll see how he feels through this afternoon, with rehab, and through tomorrow." Based on this report, there's a good chance Walker will be deemed questionable for Sunday's game against the Falcons. If he ends up limited or out this weekend, the door would be open for rookie Emmett Johnson to step into an expanded role in Week 10.

items.h: Kenneth Walker Should Rip Off Another Strong Performance If Healthy
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker popped up on the injury report Friday with groin tightness and did not practice. The late-week addition now puts his Week 10 status in question. It should be noted that the issue was listed as groin tightness and not a true injury, so the move could be precautionary. Walker rushed 18 times for 102 yards and a score in the 35-12 win over the New York Jets last week. The dynamic back also caught four passes for 41 yards and two touchdowns in the victory. After two lackluster performances against strong defenses in Week 8 and 9, Walker reminded fantasy managers just how good he is. The explosive back will now get to take on a Falcons defense that…

items.h: Three total TDs in win
items.s: Walker rushed 18 times for 102 yards and a touchdown and brought in all four targets for 41 yards and two more scores in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. Walker put together another one of his signature high-efficiency performances on the ground, averaging 5.7 yards per carry in the process. He contributed a seven-yard touchdown reception on the first play of the second quarter, and he struck again as a receiver via a 25-yard scoring grab with just over five minutes remaining in the first half. Walker capped off the highly fantasy-friendly day with his seventh rushing touchdown of the season, a two-yard run in the waning moments of the third quarter. Walker is up to 872…

items.h: Kenneth Walker III finds the end zone three times in Week 9 win
items.s: Kenneth Walker III rushed for 102 yards and one touchdown on 18 carries in a 35-12 win over the Jets. He caught all four of his targets for 41 yards and two touchdowns Walker bounced back after struggling against Denver and Seattle over the last two weeks. Walker eclipsed 100 rushing yards for the fifth time this season and logged his third game of the season with at least one rushing and one receiving touchdown. Walker and the Chiefs will take on the Falcons in Week 10.

Kenneth Walker Breaks Out of Slump in Week 9 Win
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker had 18 carries for 102 yards and a rushing touchdown and added four catches for 41 yards and two receiving touchdowns in a 35-12 win against the New York Jets in Week 9. The veteran back entered Sunday's game on a two-week slump, in which he was held to a season-low 2.6 yards per carry against the Seattle Seahawks and just 3.3 yards per carry against the Denver Broncos. Walker now has 141 carries for 770 yards and six rushing touchdowns, and 22 catches for 131 yards and two more touchdowns in his first season with Kansas City. He is RB2 in RotoBaller's position rankings and is a must-start after a bounce-back week.

items.h: Kenneth Walker Set To Break Out Of Slump In Week 9
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker handled 21 carries for 69 yards (3.3 yards per carry) and caught four passes for 15 yards in last week's loss to the Denver Broncos. The Broncos bottled up the Chiefs back, holding him to a longest run of just 10 yards. Walker has now been held to under 3.5 ypc in his last two games after being well above that mark in his blistering five-game stretch to start the season. Walker had well over 100 rushing yards in four of his first five games, and he will try to get back to that level of production against the New York Jets in Week 9. The Jets have been middle-of-the-pack against opposing running backs this season, making this a great spot for…

items.h: Kenneth Walker's Rushing Efficiency Slips During Two-Game Skid
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker hasn't shown the same explosiveness during Kansas City's two-game losing streak. He averaged 6.3 yards per carry over his first five appearances, rushing for 665 yards and scoring eight total touchdowns. Against the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos, that efficiency fell to 3.0 yards per attempt, with 105 yards on 35 carries and no touchdowns. The dip is noticeable, but it isn't a reason to bench him. Walker played 81% of the offensive snaps against Denver, handled 21 of the Chiefs' 22 running back carries, and caught four passes for the second straight game. That gave him 25 touches in Week 8, even though he finished with just 84 scrimmage…

items.h: Kenneth Walker III totals 84 yards in Week 8
items.s: Kenneth Walker III rushed 21 times for 69 yards while catching four of five targets for 15 yards in the Chiefs' 28-24 loss to the Broncos in Week 8. Walker had 25 touches and accounted for 21 of Kansas City's 24 rushing attempts. That's the good. The bad? He averaged 3.3 yards per carry and failed to score. The workload is enough to keep Walker in fantasy lineups even when the production isn't there.

items.h: Overshadowed by rookie backup in Week 8 loss
items.s: Walker carried the ball 21 times for 69 yards and caught four of five targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos. The star running back was held below 100 scrimmage yards for a second straight game, but Walker watched his rookie backup, Emmett Johnson, erupt for a 5-128-1 line on five targets and take his only carry for 15 yards. Walker is still the clear No. 1 in the Kansas City backfield, but Johnson may have earned more consistent work with Sunday's impressive effort -- touches which might come at Walker's expense. He'll head into a Week 9 meeting with the Jets second in the race for the NFL rushing crown with 770 yards, just behind Bijan Robinson's 780.

items.h: Kenneth Walker Looking To Get Back On Track At Denver
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker will face the Denver Broncos in Week 8. Walker is coming off easily his worst performance of the season facing his former team the Seattle Seahawks. The Seahawks held Walker to just 36 rushing yards on 14 carries, marking his first game with fewer than 70 rushing yards since he joined the Chiefs. Despite his down game, Walker is still second in the league in rushing, just three yards behind Bijan Robinson for the lead. Walker will get the chance to put last week behind him against the Broncos this Sunday. Walker gashed the Denver defense for 173 rushing yards and a touchdown in Week 1 as he made his debut in Kansas City. The superstar back has…

items.h: Kenneth Walker III held in check by Seahawks in Week 7
items.s: Kenneth Walker III carried the ball 14 times for 36 yards and caught four of his five targets for 21 yards in a 20-3 loss to the Seahawks in Week 7. Walker's 21 receiving yards were good enough for third on the Chiefs in receiving, which gives a good idea of how things went for the team's offense in the loss. The veteran running back has notched eight all-purpose touchdowns this season as the Chiefs' lead back. One of the top running backs in fantasy this season, Walker will be a locked-in RB1 in Week 8 vs. the Broncos.

items.h: Stymied by Seattle's elite front
items.s: Walker rushed 14 times for 36 yards while catching four of five targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks. Walker was held in check by his former team after recording at least 70 rushing yards in each of his first five games with the Chiefs. The MVP of Super LX with Seattle entered play Sunday leading the league with 665 rushing yards on 6.3 yards per carry in the 2026 regular season, but he mustered just 2.6 YPC in by far his quietest performance of the season against a Seahawks defense that hasn't allowed a 100-yard rushing performance since Week 8 of the 2024 regular season. Walker has a nice bounce-back opportunity in a Week 8 road clash with the Broncos, against whom…

items.h: Kenneth Walker Stymied in Homecoming
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker rushed 14 times for 36 yards and caught four of five targets for 21 yards in his team's 20-3 loss to the hosting Seattle Seahawks. Walker was shut down by his former team in this one. Week 7 marked the first time the fifth-year pro failed to rush for 100 yards or score a touchdown in 2026, as Kansas City's passing game stalled. Fortunately for fantasy managers, he salvaged his day with some receiving production, but it was an all-around dud for the league's leading rusher heading into the weekend. With that subpar outing behind him, Walker can turn his sights on a much more beatable Denver Broncos run defense in Week 8. Including Sunday's win…

items.h: Kenneth Walker Set For A Revenge Game
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker is set to face his former team, the Seattle Seahawks, in a battle of recent Super Bowl Champions on Sunday. Walker has been one of the most valuable backs to start the season, leading the league in rushing despite already having his bye week in Week 5. Walker rushed 19 times for 128 yards and two touchdowns in last week's win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Walker has been a feature back with the Chiefs and he will get the chance to show what he can do in that role against the Seahawks, who never seemed content to unleash him in that way. That said, the Seahawks defense is not a unit that can typically be run on. The Seattle defense is one of…

items.h: Kenneth Walker III Runs for 128 Yards, Two TDs in Week 6
items.s: Kenneth Walker III rushed 19 times for 128 yards and two touchdowns while catching two of three targets for 11 yards in the Chiefs' 22-6 win over the Chargers. Walker scored from 33 and two yards out while averaging 6.7 yards per carry. He also accounted for 19 of the Chiefs' 27 rushing attempts. There isn't much to question with that combination of workload and production. Walker remains a high-end RB1 going forward.

items.h: Week 6 winners and losers: Lawrence, Walker III impress; Robinson, Henry disappoint
items.s: Malik Nabers, Kenneth Walker III and Trevor Lawrence came up big in Week 6, while Bijan Robinson, Derrick Henry and Kyren Williams underwhelmed.

items.h: Another 100-yard effort
items.s: Walker ripped off 128 yards and two touchdowns on 19 carries and added two catches (on three targets) for 11 yards during Sunday's 22-6 win against the Chargers. Following the Chiefs' Week 5 bye, Walker continued his early-season momentum with his new team, surpassing 100 yards on the ground for the fourth time in five games in a different uniform than the Seahawks. He now boasts 133.0 rushing yards per game, which prorated over a 17-game slate (2,261) would easily go past Eric Dickerson's NFL record 2,105 from the 1984 campaign and also mark the 10th 2,000-yard season in the history of the league. Walker's next chance to strike occurs next Sunday when he visits his former teammates in…

items.h: Kenneth Walker's Historic Start to the Season Continues in Week 6
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker had 19 carries, 128 rushing yards, and two rushing touchdowns during Sunday's Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. He also converted his three targets into two catches for 11 receiving yards. After enduring running back issues for several years, the Chiefs must be thrilled to be finally getting production out of the position. In his first five games with the Chiefs, Walker has 665 rushing yards, 95 receiving yards, and eight total touchdowns. After Sunday's win, Walker became just the fourth running back in NFL history with 650+ rushing yards and six-plus rushing touchdowns through the first five games of a season. items.h: Kenneth Walker Set To Crush In Week 6
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker will take on the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 6. Walker and the rest of the team should be well-rested coming off the bye week and ready to take on a division rival in the Chargers. Los Angeles has not been a tough matchup for opposing offenses this season and their offense has not been much better as their winless record should reflect. Walker has been one of the most valuable backs in fantasy to begin the season and he should continue to handle a hefty workload after a week of rest. items.s: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker is returning from his team's bye week with a home game this week against the Chargers. He has gotten off to a fantastic start with his new team, racking up 537 rushing yards in four games with four rushing touchdowns. He has also been very involved in the passing game with 12 catches on 19 targets for 84 receiving yards and two more touchdowns. items.h: Kenneth Walker III runs for 177 yards, two TDs in Week 4
items.s: Kenneth Walker III carried the ball 22 times for 177 yards and two touchdowns while catching his lone target for a two-yard gain in a 30-27 win over the Raiders in Week 4. Walker notched his third multi-touchdown game of the season in what has been an impressive start to the year. The veteran running back found the end zone on rushes of two and 22 yards in the win. Overall, Walker has 537 rushing yards and six all-purpose touchdowns on the year. A locked-in high-end RB1 the rest of the way, he will be on bye in Week 5 before taking on the Chargers in Week 6.

items.h: Walker rushed 22 times for 177 yards and two touchdowns while catching his only target for two yards in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders.
items.s: Walker's two touchdowns came just 19 seconds apart in the fourth quarter, as he gave Kansas City the lead with a two-yard touchdown run and added a 22-yard touchdown run to create some breathing room after the Raiders fumbled the ensuing kickoff. The free-agent addition has paid immediate dividends for his new team, racking up 537 rushing yards and six total touchdowns through four games with the Chiefs. Walker has handled heavy workloads early in the season and will have a chance to rest up during a Week 5 bye before the 4-0 Chiefs host the Chargers in Week 6.

items.h: Walker rushed 18 times for 70 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for three yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-10 win over the Dolphins.
items.s: Walker recorded a rushing touchdown and receiving touchdown in the same game for the second time in three outings as a member of the Chiefs. He capped Kansas City's opening drive with a 10-yard touchdown run just 2:06 into the game before adding a five-yard touchdown reception in the second quarter. Walker has racked up 76 touches while thriving in a workhorse role for his new team heading into a Week 4 road tilt in Vegas.

Walker wasn't shabby on the ground by any stretch, either, and he's quickly amassed 290 rushing yards and his 60-yard touchdown in Week 1 as a runner while also offering plenty of value as a pass catcher with a 9-79-1 line on 16 targets. items.s: Walker paid immediate dividends in his Chiefs regular-season debut, finding the end zone via a fourth-down, 60-yard run around left end early in the third quarter before adding a nifty two-yard scoring grab on a shovel pass from Patrick Mahomes within the first minute of the final period. items.h: Walker (ankle) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star reports.
items.s: Walker dealt with some swelling around his ankle last week due to some cleat issues, but the star running back is back in action Wednesday with 12 days to go before the Chiefs open their season at home against the Broncos on Monday, Sept. 14. After splitting duties with Zach Charbonnet (knee) in Seattle, Walker is expected to operate as a three-down workhorse with Kansas City this season. Only fifth-round rookie Emmett Johnson and 2025 seventh-rounder Brashard Smith round out the depth chart behind Walker.

items.h: Walker is experiencing swelling around his ankle but is expected to "be fine," Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports.
items.s: It was reported Tuesday that Walker was dealing with a foot injury, and head coach Andy Reid clarified a day later that he is actually dealing with an ankle issue. Reid did not express any concern about about Walker's status, so it appears he is not facing any sort of extended absence.
